key_insight: SUPRA-Tex improves single-image 3D generation by separating material estimation, surface alignment, and 3D completion, so the final textured mesh stays both visually faithful and physically consistent. This helps preserve fine image details while avoiding the artifacts common in multi-view fusion approaches.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of dressing a 3D mesh with relightable textures from a single reference image without losing fine details or introducing inconsistencies across views.
method: Decouples the pipeline into visible-material estimation, surface alignment, and observation-guided 3D completion.
Aligns texture/material predictions to the target 3D surface to reduce cross-view mismatch and artifacts.
Uses observation guidance to complete unseen regions while preserving reference-image details.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a more reliable way to generate textured 3D assets from minimal input, improving quality for graphics, virtual try-on, games, and AR/VR workflows. It also highlights a design pattern—explicitly separating alignment from completion—that can generalize to other 3D reconstruction tasks.
